title: Construction Contract Payment 2026: Documents, Deadlines, Late Interest
desc: Construction contract payment 2026 under Decree 210/2026/ND-CP: payment by contract type, payment dossier, the 14-working-day deadline and late interest.
summary: Construction contract payment rules from 1 July 2026: general principles, payment dossiers by contract type, payment deadlines and the duty to pay interest on late payment.
body: Disputes between homeowners and contractors often begin with payment: which instalment, what papers are needed, what if it is late. This article summarises Article 87 of the Construction Law 2025 and Articles 28 and 29 of Decree 210/2026/ND-CP.

Payment must be consistent with the contract type, contract price and contract conditions; the parties agree the method, timing, dossier, and conditions for payment or interim payment (Point a, Clause 2, Article 87 of the Construction Law).
The employer must pay the full amount and on time for each payment, after deducting advances and agreed retentions (Point b, Clause 2).
The currency of payment is Vietnamese dong; use of foreign currency must comply with foreign exchange law (Point c, Clause 2).
The form of payment (cash, bank transfer, etc.) is agreed by the parties (Clause 1, Article 28 of Decree 210).
For public-investment and PPP projects, Clause 4, Article 28 provides specifically; for private housing the same approach can be applied when drafting the contract:

Lump-sum contracts: payment as a percentage of the contract price or of the item price corresponding to the agreed stages; no detailed confirmation of completed quantities is required, except for variations outside the contract scope.

Fixed unit-price and adjustable unit-price contracts: payment on the actual completed and accepted quantities (including increases and decreases) multiplied by the contract unit price or the adjusted unit price.
Variation quantities without a unit price: payment under a supplementary agreement settled by both parties before the work is done.
3. What does the payment dossier contain?

The dossier is prepared by the contractor, confirmed by the employer's representative (or the consultant, if any) and the contractor's representative; its components are agreed by the parties (Clause 1, Article 29). For a lump-sum contract, the main components are (Clause 2, Article 29):
An acceptance record for the quantities and work completed in the payment stage (no detailed quantity confirmation needed);
A calculation sheet of the value of work arising outside the contract scope (if any);
The contractor's payment request: the completed value, the variation value, the advance deduction and the amount requested.

For a fixed unit-price contract, the acceptance record is replaced by a record of actual completed quantities, with a calculation sheet for work that has no unit price (Clause 3). The employer and related agencies may not add dossier requirements contrary to the contract so as to obstruct payment (Clause 14).

For public-investment and PPP projects, the maximum payment period is 14 working days from the date the employer receives a complete and valid payment dossier (Point l, Clause 4, Article 28); for ODA and foreign-loan projects, international treaties apply. For private works, the period is agreed by the two parties – it is advisable to state a specific number of days.

An employer that pays late must pay interest on the late amount for the period of delay. The interest rate is agreed by the parties; if not agreed, the overdue interest rate announced by the commercial bank where the contractor holds its account applies (Clause 5, Article 28). The Civil Code also provides for the obligation to pay interest on late payment of money (Article 357).

Prolonged late payment can also lead to suspension or termination of the contract: for public-investment and PPP projects, the contractor may suspend work when the employer is more than 28 days late (Point a, Clause 2, Article 26); an employer that fails to pay more than 56 days after the due date commits a serious breach, unless otherwise agreed (Point d, Clause 2, Article 27).

This article is a summary for reference only and does not replace the legal texts. The 14-working-day deadline and the detailed rules by contract type in Clause 4, Article 28 and Clauses 2–12, Article 29 are mandatory for public-investment and PPP projects. For contracts signed and being performed before 1 July 2026 (projects not using public-investment capital), the parties may agree to apply Decree 210/2026/ND-CP; if they cannot agree, the rules at the time of signing apply (Clause 2, Article 33).
